subject: Edge diversion notice and follow-up: targeted regional reroute (EU/APAC)
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Li <samantha@shoplify.io>, ops-team@shoplify.io
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 17 May 2029 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Edge diversion notice and follow-up: targeted regional reroute (EU/APAC)

Hi Samantha / Shoplify ops team,

Quick heads-up: between 08:50–09:10 UTC we observed a cloud provider peering disruption affecting ingress to our eu-west-1 and apac-east-1 edge POPs for a subset of customers. To protect request success rates we initiated an automated diversion that routed affected traffic to nearby healthy regions (primarily us-west-2 for APAC-impacted tenants and eu-central-1 for certain EU zones).

What you may have seen: 5–15% request errors for a short window and increased 95th%-ile latency for sessions that were rerouted (~30–80ms additional, depending on geographic path). We did not see data-plane integrity issues (no dropped tokens) but some requests experienced transient 502/504s while the route converged.

Immediate customer action:
- No action required to continue serving; our diversion is automatic.
- If you prefer strict regional affinity, please confirm and we can switch your account to a strict-fail policy (note: stricter affinity increases error rate during provider flaps).
- To opt into cross-region fallback (recommended), enable the endpoint flag: enable_cross_region_fallback=true in your Console -> Routing -> Advanced.

We've attached a condensed reroute_playbook_v1.pdf with short instructions for validation and an example curl-based endpoint check you can run.

I'm copying Ben (ops) and Marissa (product) who are tracking recovery and next steps. We'll send a brief post-incident summary and propose a follow-up call to review long-term mitigations.

Apologies for the disruption — will follow up with a timeline and proposed mitigations within the hour.

Thanks,
Rachel Kim
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
rachel.kim@redwood.ai

Attachment: reroute_playbook_v1.pdf (PDF, 120KB)

Subject: Re: Edge diversion notice and follow-up: targeted regional reroute (EU/APAC)

Thanks Rachel — appreciate the quick note. A couple quick questions from our ops team:

1) Do you have a concrete ETA for when the eu-west-1 peering will be fully stable?
2) Will session stickiness (our KV cache-backed conversational sessions) be preserved when traffic is rerouted? Our nightly batch jobs run at 04:00 UTC and we want to ensure they're not impacted.
3) Also, given we saw increased errors during the window, what is the process for SLA credit requests?

If helpful I can jump on a brief call with Ben/Marissa to go over our routing config — we prefer to understand permanence of any changes before toggling flags.

—Samantha
Samantha Li
Head of Platform Operations, Shoplify
samantha@shoplify.io
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>

Subject: Fwd: Re: Edge diversion notice and follow-up: targeted regional reroute (EU/APAC)

FYI — quick ops notes and answers to Samantha:

On Fri, May 17, 2029 at 09:23 AM Samantha Li <samantha@shoplify.io> wrote:
> Thanks Rachel — appreciate the quick note. A couple quick questions from our ops team:
>
> 1) Do you have a concrete ETA for when the eu-west-1 peering will be fully stable?
> 2) Will session stickiness (our KV cache-backed conversational sessions) be preserved when traffic is rerouted? Our nightly batch jobs run at 04:00 UTC and we want to ensure they're not impacted.
> 3) Also, given we saw increased errors during the window, what is the process for SLA credit requests?

Answers / actions:
- ETA: the provider reported convergence at ~09:10 UTC. Our monitoring shows normal request success rates resumed by 09:15 UTC. I will attach a short KV/cache verification checklist (kv-cache-checklist.txt) that Marissa and I used to validate state consistency.
- Stickiness: short answer — in most cases yes. We maintain KV affinity and the runtime attempts to warm the remote cache during reroute, but there can be a cold-read penalty on first request after migration (up to ~120ms). For session-critical workloads we recommend setting read-retry=2 and enabling prefix-cache for high-frequency keys.
- SLA credits: forward SLA requests to support@redwood.ai with the incident id (INC-20290517-01). We will triage and provide a candidate credit; final approvals require Account + Revenue review. Rachel — please capture Shoplify's impacted window and any token counts they want considered.

Planned customer-facing steps:
1) Rachel to confirm whether Shoplify wants cross-region fallback enabled (opt-in).
2) Marissa to prepare a short postmortem and remediation plan and propose a 30-min review call.
3) Ops to run KV validation for Shoplify on the next maintenance window and share results.

Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Operations Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Subject: Post-incident summary and next steps — 2029-05-17 EU/APAC edge reroute (INC-20290517-01)

Hi Samantha / Shoplify ops,

Thanks again for patience while we completed the internal review. Below is a concise post-incident summary, impact assessment, and recommended next steps. We propose a 30-minute review call this Wednesday to walk through the details and answer questions.

Timeline (UTC):
- 08:49 — Provider peering anomaly begins impacting a subset of routes into eu-west-1 / apac-east-1.
- 08:50 — Redwood automated routing detects elevated error rates and executes diversion policy for impacted tenants.
- 08:50–09:10 — Diversion active; affected tenants see transient 502/504 spikes and increased p95 latency (30–80ms).
- 09:10 — Provider reports partial convergence; Redwood begins routing back where path health meets thresholds.
- 09:15 — Metrics show request success rates returned to baseline for Shoplify.

Root cause: a peering flap at the provider edge (external to Redwood) caused path instability for a subset of our edge POPs. Our automated diversion logic worked as designed and preserved availability for affected workloads, but the transient errors you observed occurred during convergence.

Customer impact (Shoplify):
- Window: 08:50–09:15 UTC on 2029-05-17.
- User-facing errors: short spike of 502/504s for specific EU/APAC users; estimated impacted token volume provided on request.
- Batch jobs: based on your note, nightly batches at 04:00 UTC were not within the impacted window. No reprocessing recommended unless you detect anomalies in job logs.

Mitigations we’ve applied:
- Tuned the diversion thresholds to lower false-positive reroutes for small-scale peering jitter.
- Added an additional warm-read attempt to KV migration path to reduce cold-read latency on first rerouted requests.
- Implemented an internal runbook improvement: ops will broadcast an immediate targeted advisory to affected accounts within 10 minutes of detection (we missed shaving a couple minutes here).

Recommended customer actions:
1) If you want us to enable cross-region fallback for your account we will flip the flag and monitor for one week — Rachel, please confirm.
2) Set read-retry=2 and prefix-cache for session keys as a short-term mitigation for cold reads.
3) Validate application-side retry/backoff behavior around 502/504s during peak windows.

SLA credits & next steps:
- To request SLA credit please reply to support@redwood.ai with INC-20290517-01 and an estimate of impacted token volume/time. Rachel will help coordinate the request and expedite approvals.
- We are offering Shoplify a one-time account credit equivalent to two days of inference usage for the impacted traffic while we finalize the credit calculation; if that works for you we can expedite paperwork.

Attachments: postmortem_summary.docx (contains full timeline, raw metric graphs, and runbook changes).

Proposed meeting slots (30 min): Wed May 22 — 09:00 UTC / 14:00 UTC / 20:00 UTC. Please let us know which works best.

Apologies for the disruption — we take these events seriously and have prioritized the follow-ups listed above.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Product Manager, Reliability | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
